goldens.comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.

The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication.rationale:
Yes. In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` the migration interpolates `h` directly into a raw SQL string:

```rb
execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"
```

`h` comes from the `site_settings` row `embeddable_hosts` and is not escaped/quoted safely. If any host value contains a single quote or other SQL-special characters, the migration can fail (syntax error) or, in the worst case, allow SQL injection during migration execution. This is a concrete defect introduced by the diff (raw SQL with unescaped interpolation).

Yes. In `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update` and `#destroy`, the record is fetched via `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first`. If no record exists for that `id`, `host` will be `nil`. `update` then calls `save_host(host)`, which immediately does `host.host = ...` and `host.category_id = ...`, raising `NoMethodError` on `nil`. `destroy` similarly calls `host.destroy` on a possible `nil`. This is a real correctness defect (request can 500 instead of returning 404/invalid params).

In `update`, the controller does `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then unconditionally calls `save_host(host)`. If the record isn’t found, `host` will be `nil`, and `save_host` immediately does `host.host = ...` (around line 24), causing a `NoMethodError` and a 500 instead of a proper 404/JSON error. This is a real, verifiable correctness bug introduced/present in the diff.

In `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host`, line 17 queries `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first` but the bound parameter `host` is not lowercased. If the incoming URL has an uppercase hostname (valid in URLs; hostnames are case-insensitive), `lower(host) = 'EvilTrout.com'` will not match `eviltrout.com` in a case-sensitive comparison, defeating the intent of using `lower(host)`. It should compare against `host.downcase` (or `lower(?)`). This is a correctness bug in the diff.

The diff removes `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` and the `embeddable_hosts` / `embed_category` site settings, but also consistently replaces their usage with the new `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` and per-host category logic (`EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` in `TopicEmbed`, and host checks in `EmbedController`/`TopicRetriever`). The migration copies the old settings into the new table and then deletes the old settings. There is no remaining reference in the diff to the removed method/settings that would cause a breakage, so the finding (as stated) does not identify a verifiable defect introduced by this change.

The proposed finding only names two spec files (`spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb` and `spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb`) but does not describe any concrete issue (bug, failure, incorrect expectation, etc.) to verify against the diff. With no stated problem, there is nothing verifiable to judge as a real defect introduced by the changes.

The “proposed finding” does not actually state any issue—only a file path and line number are provided, with no claim about what is wrong. Without an identified problem, there is nothing verifiable in the diff to confirm as a real defect.

In `Admin::EmbeddingController`, the `update` action (lines 10-12) does not update anything—it ignores incoming params and simply re-renders the existing `@embedding` object, identical to `show`. Given the diff also adds a client-side `saveChanges()` action that calls `this.get('embedding').update({})` and routes a `PUT /admin/customize/embedding`, this means any attempted “save” via that endpoint will be a no-op while still returning success, which is a real correctness/behavior defect.

In `EmbeddableHost` the `before_validation` callback unconditionally calls `self.host.sub!` twice. Because callbacks run before validations, `self.host` can be `nil` (e.g., a new record created without `host` set, or bad/missing params), which would raise `NoMethodError` instead of producing a normal validation error. The diff does not guard with `return if host.blank?` / `host&.` etc., so this is a real correctness/robustness bug introduced by the callback at lines 6-7.
